production_observation.root_cause: The acquisition task dispatched the independent document task before checking whether the same tick was a due fixed publication. Publication document_index held a documents.sqlite BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction while document results tried to commit.

behavior.publish_only: Do not dispatch documents before publication. Acquire documents.lock without waiting before any publication scan and hold it through the complete publish. Dispatch once after a successful publication returns.
behavior.documents_active: Return publish_deferred_documents_active without changing CURRENT or the publication checkpoint, do not dispatch another document task, and retry on the next tick.
behavior.failed_publish: Release documents.lock, do not start a competing document task, and leave the existing publication checkpoint pending for the next retry.
behavior.planning_or_acquisition: Invoke the document dispatch hook before planning or acquisition so the two dedicated workers retain their existing parallelism.
behavior.legacy_every_tick: Because every legacy tick publishes, dispatch documents only after acquisition and publication complete.
behavior.disabled_or_blocked_tick: After a normal non-deferred tick return, perform the same bounded document dispatch and let the document worker enforce its existing authority, enable and disk gates.

limits_unchanged: two download workers and one parse phase

production_acceptance_required: Deploy only after both dedicated queues are drained and source/Git are aligned.
Observe an active document task causing one fast publish_deferred_documents_active result without changing CURRENT or the checkpoint.
Observe the following due automatic publish below the 160 second soft limit while it holds documents.lock.
Verify the successful publish dispatches exactly one subsequent document task.
Observe later non-publication acquisition and document work running in parallel.
Verify no new database-is-locked document failure in the acceptance window and both workers remain healthy.
